turns.content: Ugh, okay so my cat-sitting direct deposit is four days late now and I'm spiraling a little lol 😅 I think I submitted the wrong voided check form on day one and now I'm low-key worried Chloe is dragging her feet on purpose?? But it's literally just $85 so I refuse to make it a big deal. Can you write me a quick two-sentence text to her just checking in? Something friendly but not pushy!

Four days late on money you've earned is annoying, and it makes sense that your brain went to "is this on purpose" — but there's a much simpler explanation sitting right there: you think you sent the wrong voided check form. That alone would stall a deposit, and it's the kind of thing that's easy to fix and easy to forget to mention.

I'd also gently flag the "it's only $85 so I won't make it a big deal" move. The amount doesn't change whether it's reasonable to ask. You can be completely casual and still follow up.

Here's a text:

> Hey Chloe! Just checking in on the cat-sitting payment — I think I may have sent you the wrong voided check form on day one, so that might be holding things up. Happy to resend whatever you need, just let me know!

That's friendly, gives her an easy out, and puts the fix in your hands rather than making it about her being slow.

One practical note: if she doesn't respond in a day or two, a short second message asking whether she got the first one is fine — texts do get buried. And if you can, send the correct form proactively rather than waiting to be asked; it removes the one concrete obstacle you already know about.

Okay but you're probably right that it's just the wrong form lol 😅 Still, a tiny part of me is like... what if she's mad I messed up and is making me wait?? I know that's dumb though!! Anyway your draft is perfect, super chill. I'll send that. Thanks!! ✨

Glad the draft works. One thing worth saying, though: the worry isn't dumb. You're waiting on money with no explanation, and your brain filled the gap with a story — that's a normal thing brains do, not a character flaw.

Where I'd push back is on treating the story as likely. You have a concrete, boring explanation for the delay that you yourself identified, and no actual evidence of her being upset. "She's mad and punishing me" requires her to be annoyed *and* to express it by withholding $85 — that's two assumptions stacked on top of each other, versus one form that probably didn't process. If she were mad, most people would just say so.

So: send the text, and if you can, go ahead and send the correct form now rather than waiting for her to ask. That way you've cleared the one obstacle you know exists, and whatever happens next is actually informative instead of guesswork.

If she replies normally, that settles it. If she goes quiet for a couple of days, a short "hey, did my last message come through?" is a reasonable next step — not pushy, just following up on your own money.

Alright I literally just sent your draft and she replied almost immediately saying "no worries at all! Let me check and get back to you" so... now I feel kinda silly for the whole conspiracy theory lol 😅 Still no money yet though!! Should I just wait for her to get back to me or send the correct form now like you said?

Her reply is the answer to the question you were actually worried about — "no worries at all" is not what someone who's annoyed and withholding money says. So the conspiracy theory is dead, and you don't need to feel silly about it. You had a real gap in information and your brain filled it; now you have better information.

On the form: send it now. You already told her you might have sent the wrong one, so following through isn't pushy — it's just completing the thing you offered. It also means she doesn't have to come back and ask you for it, which is the step where things tend to stall.

Something short:

> Here's the correct form just in case — let me know if you need anything else from me!

Then wait. She said she'd check and get back to you, and that's a reasonable thing to let her do. If a couple of days pass with no money and no word, a brief "hey, any update on the deposit?" is fine — you're not being demanding, you're just tracking money you earned.

Oh wait so she replied that fast?? That's actually such a relief omg 😅 Okay I'll send the correct form right now!! You're right it's way better to just get it done than wait for her to ask again. Thanks for talking me down from my weird conspiracy ledge lol 😂✨

Ha — glad it landed. For what it's worth, you didn't need much talking down; you spotted the likely cause yourself on day one, you just didn't fully believe it. That's a decent instinct to trust more next time.

Send the form, then let it sit. If nothing shows up in a couple of days, a one-line "any update on the deposit?" is all you need.
Okay I sent the form and she said "got it, will process today!" so crisis averted lol 😅 Thanks for talking me down from my weird suspicion ledge!! ✨

Nice — that's about as clean a resolution as you could get. You flagged the likely cause, sent the fix, and it's moving.

Small takeaway worth keeping: your first read ("I probably sent the wrong form") was right, and the suspicion was the part that didn't hold up. Next time money's late, lead with the boring explanation and check it — it's faster and less stressful than the alternative.

Nothing more to do here unless the deposit doesn't actually land today. If it doesn't, a short "hey, just checking — did the deposit go through?" is all you'd need.
